purpose: Minecraft-implementable Oil Engine art proposals; not exported runtime assets

variants.prompt:
Create a highly practical Minecraft Java mod machine mockup, a Blockbench-style low-poly asset render, not a realistic illustration. Landscape design sheet with large three-quarter view on the left and smaller SIDE and FRONT orthographic views on the right, all exactly the same machine. Plain warm gray studio background, soft ambient lighting, sharp edges. Title only "A â€” EXPOSED IRON". Machine: compact circa-1900 hot-bulb oil engine, sturdy beautiful industrial composition, readable at Minecraft player distance. On a low dark riveted steel slab bed approximately THREE Minecraft blocks wide by THREE blocks deep, less than THREE blocks tall. Show subtle one-meter grid on ground for actual scale. Primary silhouette: a horizontal iron cylinder aligned front-to-back on the right, and one exposed open eight-sided flywheel on its left with four broad spokes. Crankshaft axle runs side-to-side; a visible simple connecting rod joins crank to piston with credible clearance. Every support directly touches the base. Modest protected hot bulb at cylinder far end, ONE narrow straight exhaust with right angle top; a small brass lubricator. Front controller is an inset readable small brass plate and simple mechanical lever. Separate square fuel and lubricant connection ports on opposing bed sides. No tall pedestal, no giant central solid blob. Air and negative space between cylinder, bed, flywheel, and connecting rod.
STRICT MODELING LANGUAGE: actual Minecraft-compatible geometry, mostly axis-aligned cuboids, some cubes rotated 45 degrees, only eight-sided approximations of round parts. Large simple forms, about 40â€“70 cuboids total; no tessellated smooth cylinders, curved pipes, tiny bolts, complex bevels or filigree. Rivets, panel seams and wear are painted square pixels in the texture, not separate geometry. Texture density visually consistent with Faithful 32x Minecraft: sharp deliberate pixel clusters, flat restrained iron-gray base colors, sparse dark seams and pale edge pixels, a little warm brass, no random photographic noise or PBR. No painterly shading or smooth gradients baked into texture. Bright enough iron to read under shaders. Show actual textured game-ready-looking geometry, not photoreal concept-art aspirations. Do not depict a boiler, steam tank, electric motor, extra engines, gears everywhere, UI overlays, dynamic flames, smooth rubber hoses, or futuristic equipment. Smaller views must keep identical geometry and materials. This is a feasible ART PROPOSAL not an engineering dimensional blueprint; only labels A EXPOSED IRON / SIDE / FRONT.
variants.review: Readable cuboid/octagonal forms and supported base. Exposed linkage is schematic: the pictured rod meets the hub rather than an offset crank, and view alignment is not an engineering reference. Correct mechanical layout in Blockbench before animation. Port positions and apparent footprint are illustrative.

variants.prompt:
Minecraft Java mod machine design mockup: a practical low-poly Blockbench asset with visible crisp pixel textures. Landscape sheet: one LARGE three-quarter orthographic render taking 75% width, and one smaller opposite-side view. Plain warm-gray backdrop, soft Minecraft-like ambient illumination, no cinematic atmosphere. Title "B â€” MARINE ENCLOSED". Depict the same compact 1890â€“1910 HOT-BULB OIL ENGINE in both views, modest rugged elegance: slate teal enamel main crankcase, medium gray cast iron, restrained brass handles and thin copper oil line made of straight cuboid segments. A low riveted dark steel base THREE Minecraft blocks wide by THREE deep; machine at most 2.5 blocks high. HORIZONTAL cylinder points front-to-back on the right. Left-side flywheel vertical in a front-to-back plane, horizontal axle runs left-right into the crankcase. An open eight-sided wheel roughly 1.5 Minecraft blocks across, four broad straight spokes; NO visible connecting rod across the wheel hub: crank and piston linkage contained inside the rectangular teal crankcase, service panel has a readable small square inspection hatch. Wheel mostly exposed with ONE simple cuboid protective top bar attached to substantial supports outside its rotation envelope. Important flywheel rests on real axle bearings, no floating parts. Stepped cuboid shroud encloses hot bulb on far end, small orange STARTUP window only, one short vertical exhaust at rear. Front mechanical control plate flush with casing, simple brass lever. Two simple square supply ports on opposite side faces of base with one tiny drop pictogram each. Everything reads as a single coherent, solidly supported machine with very few parts. Engine suitable for either workshop or ship hold.
STRICT Minecraft geometry: cuboids and 45-degree rotated cuboids, octagonal round forms only, faceted surfaces with no bevel chains. Target about 35â€“55 cuboids, trim and rivets drawn in pixels, not modeled dots. No continuous curved pipes, fine wirework, gears, boiler, gauges everywhere, glossy PBR, photographic metal grain. TEXTURE STYLE: pixel-painted planar faces approximately 32 texels per meter, solid subdued teal panels with sparse intentional seam/edge pixels, matching iron sides, clear broad color areas, visually quiet textures, no checker patterns. Every view must retain same component arrangement. Strong resemblance to an actual rendered Minecraft mod model, not a photoreal sculpture assembled from tiny voxels. Make it feasible to recreate directly in Blockbench. All visible shadowing from model lighting, avoid baked dramatic gradients. The low base and exposed wheel make its scale clear, subtle one-block floor grid only, no dimension annotations or human figures. This is an art proposal, not an implemented asset.
variants.review: Preferred candidate for coherent casing and simple animated wheel; hidden linkage reduces visual/mechanical complexity. Simplify the oversized overhead frame, lower base to the existing slab bed, reduce surface noise and protect wheel clearance during blockout. Startup glow must not persist during normal operation. Not user-selected yet.
